bullets.title: June PPI -0.3% MoM, 5.5% YoY — Both Prints Sharply Below Consensus
bullets.body: June PPI fell 0.3% MoM (est. 0.0%, prior +1.1%) and rose only 5.5% YoY (est. 6.2%), with core PPI at +4.7% YoY vs. +5.1% expected. Nearly two-thirds of the monthly goods decline was driven by gasoline -12%. Empire State Manufacturing simultaneously beat: +15.6 vs. +9.2 est., pointing to re-accelerating regional demand even as input costs cool.

bullets.title: Fed Hawkish Hold: Cook Signals Ready to Act if Disinflation Stalls; September Hike Window Open
bullets.body: Governor Cook said it's prudent to wait 'a bit more time' before cutting, but she is 'prepared to act' if inflation doesn't decelerate soon — interpreted by analysts as a September hike optionality rather than a guaranteed cut. Risk assessment has shifted toward higher inflation since last summer, with AI capex, tariffs, and Middle East conflict flagged as upside price risks. Fed funds futures now price >50% odds of no cuts through September.

bullets.title: Warsh Confirmation Hearings: Hawkish Lean, AI-Price Skeptic, Balance Sheet Hawk
bullets.body: Nominee Warsh kept rates as primary monetary tool, wants a small balance sheet reserved for crises only, and declined to label AI-driven demand pressures as inflationary — distancing himself from more hawkish colleagues on that specific point. He acknowledged 63 months of above-target inflation and said June CPI/PPI showed improvement. Warsh also expressed openness to bank stress test reform.

bullets.title: Fed Williams Sees Inflation Peaked at 4%, Targets 3.25% Year-End, 2% by 2028
bullets.body: Williams called current ~4% inflation 'unquestionably too high' but cited 'encouraging' signs it has peaked and expects gradual decline to 3.25% by year-end and 2% by 2028. GDP growth guided to 2%-2.25% this year; labor market described as solid and stable. He noted Middle East conflict poses 'significant risks' but the US economy has absorbed these 'fairly well.'

bullets.title: Goldman Flags Clear Hyperscaler vs. Semi Rotation; HFs Net Selling Tech at 98th Pct
bullets.body: Goldman's desk notes a 'clear theme of buying hyperscalers vs. selling semis': the Mag7 basket outperforming NDX by nearly 3% while the semiconductor/memory pair basket (GSPRHIMO) is down 6.5% on the session. HFs were -15% better for sale in tech/comms — 98th percentile over the past year — while LOs were marginally better to buy.

bullets.title: Semiconductor ETF SMH Down 3.7% Intraday; SNDK -11%, DELL -13% to Session Lows
bullets.body: SMH fell 3.7% from the open despite a green start, extending the sector's recent correction. SanDisk extended losses to -11% session low and Dell sank to -13%, its worst single-day drop since April 2025. DRAM prices facing 20%+ hike expectations next quarter, but market is selling memory on rotation despite strong LTA activity (SNDK signing deals with META and MU).

bullets.title: NVDA CEO Huang in Tokyo Denies Vera Rubin Delays; Says Production Already in 'Giant Volumes'
bullets.body: Jensen Huang stated 'the reports are not true' on AI server delays, confirming Vera Rubin is in production with large volumes incoming. Separately, millions in NVDA put sweepers were detected intraday, and the stock has reclaimed its 50-DMA after testing the 200-DMA weeks ago.

bullets.title: Apple Hunting AI Chip Acquisitions; M2 Ultra Falls Short for AI Workloads
bullets.body: Per The Information, Apple approached multiple chip startups to gauge acquisition interest, targeting server chip development for AI deployments. Simultaneously, Apple's M2 Ultra chips have reportedly fallen short for advanced AI workloads, forcing reliance on Nvidia — suggesting M&A urgency. AAPL hit new all-time highs and is within $250B of $5T market cap.

bullets.title: Iran Escalation: Trump Warns Expanded Strikes Next Week; Hormuz Control, Kuwait Explosions
bullets.body: Trump told Fox News strikes against Iran will expand next week; US spokesperson said the US 'can attack anywhere, anytime.' Iran's top negotiator Qalibaf gave multiple statements emphasizing national security hinges on Hormuz control and characterizing the situation as an 'existential war.' Explosions were also reported in Kuwait following reported Iranian drone assault. Treasury sanctioned IRGC-linked weapons procurement networks.

bullets.title: SPY Options Structure: $2B+ Put Wall at 750 Held as Support; Call Wall at 755
bullets.body: The SPY 750 strike (described as a billion-dollar put wall) acted as intraday support and produced a bounce. A $2B+ call wall is building at 755. Bears tested the 750 level, described as 'the final line of support for bulls before a potential sharp decline.'

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO as Early as October; $965B Valuation After $65B Round
bullets.body: Bloomberg reports Anthropic is planning to hold IPO investor meetings in coming weeks with a target of going public as early as October. The company's latest financing valued it at $965B, with $65B raised in May. IPO volume more broadly has hit its highest level since 2021, driven by AI deals.

bullets.title: NY Data Center Moratorium Creates AI Infrastructure Choke Point; Trump and Energy Secretary Criticize Decision
bullets.body: New York Governor Hochul's moratorium on data centers is drawing sharp criticism from Trump (who filed to buy up to $1M in EQIX) and Energy Secretary Wright, who argued data centers are a solution to high electricity prices. NY has roughly 1/6th of Virginia's data centers and nearly double the electricity rates. Pennsylvania separately enacted stricter oversight for data center operations.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: US Hyperscaler Capex to Exceed $1.2T by 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley projects aggregate US hyperscaler capital expenditures will surpass $1.2 trillion by 2027. B200 compute pricing is turning up sharply in early July, and Goldman separately warned hyperscaler debt issuance skews risk to the downside with a 'as good as it gets' framing.

bullets.title: Financials Sector Overbought for 22 Consecutive Days
bullets.body: The financials sector has registered overbought readings for 22 straight sessions, the longest such streak in recent memory. No reversal catalyst was cited but the extreme reading flags technical stretched conditions for the group.

bullets.title: Uber Nearing €12.5B Deal to Acquire Delivery Hero; Announcement Expected Thursday
bullets.body: Uber is in advanced negotiations to acquire Delivery Hero for approximately €12.5 billion, with an announcement expected as early as Thursday. As part of the deal, Delivery Hero would divest its Turkish unit Yemeksepeti and several European businesses to an investment firm.

bullets.title: Alibaba Qwen AI to Integrate into Apple Intelligence in China; BABA +5.7%
bullets.body: Reports that Alibaba's Qwen AI model will be integrated into Apple Intelligence for the China market drove US-listed Alibaba shares up 5.7%. This follows Apple's previously reported pivot to Alibaba as its China AI partner.

bullets.title: Bank of Canada Holds at 2.25%, Slashes 2026 Growth Forecast to 0.7%, Drops Rate-Cut Language
bullets.body: BOC held rates at 2.25% as expected but cut its 2026 GDP growth forecast sharply to 0.7% from 1.2% in April, while raising 2026 inflation to 2.5% from 2.3%. Importantly, the BOC dropped both its reference to consecutive hikes and forward language around future cuts, signaling a genuinely data-dependent stance. Macklem flagged Middle East conflicts and US trade as biggest risks.

bullets.title: US Crude Inventories Draw 1.7MB; SPR Hits Lowest Since April 1983
bullets.body: EIA showed crude inventories fell 1.7MB (est. -1.96MB, prior +3MB). The SPR dropped 2.985MB in the past week to 317MB, the lowest level since April 1983. Distillates built +4.6MB while gasoline drew 1.5MB. WTI trading near $78/bbl intraday lows despite a 15%+ rally from recent lows; June average tracking at $80 vs. $82 in May.

bullets.title: DTCC Launches Pilot to Tokenize Russell 1000 Stocks and Treasuries with 40+ Firms
bullets.body: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation is launching a pilot with nearly 40 financial institutions — including JPMorgan, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and Vanguard — to tokenize equities (including Microsoft and Treasury ETFs) on blockchain infrastructure. NYSE is also involved in the trial.

bullets.title: Equity Valuations Relative to Bonds at Historic Extremes; Stretched but Momentum Intact
bullets.body: One macro strategist noted equity valuations relative to bonds are now more extreme than 2000 dot-com and 1929 peaks. Separately, a regime framework noted valuations are 'super stretched' and inflation is high but falling, while trend, momentum, and breadth remain good-to-excellent — a positive regime that still supports equities despite the stretched starting point.
